about: What GitHub answers a GitHub Actions job that asks for its OIDC token, as captured from a real run (source). Both clients' tests answer from it through a stub GitHub: packages/envoy/internal/cipherclient/githubactions_test.go and packages/cipher-client/src/__tests__/github-actions-identity.test.ts.
request_url is what the run printed of ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL: its scheme and its query's keys. request_token_bytes is the length of ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN.

answer is GitHub's answer to the job's own request token, asked for audience. Its body's value is the placeholder ${jwt}: each suite signs jwt.header and jwt.claims with a key of its own and answers that token in its place, with a jti of its own in each token, as GitHub mints one per request.
Values that name the account are example values of the same form, and the branch the run was on is refs/heads/main here. A value of the form <name> is one the run printed and this file does not keep.
refused is GitHub's answer to the wrong request token refused.request_token. no_audience is the aud of a token asked for with no audience parameter.

source.workflow: capture-oidc-shape, a one-off workflow on a scratch branch that was deleted after the run
commands: python3 -c 'import os,urllib.parse as p; u=p.urlsplit(os.environ["ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL"]); print(u.scheme, bool(u.query), sorted(p.parse_qs(u.query)))'

a curl GET of $ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL with &audience=https://cipher.example added, the job's own ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN as its bearer, writing the body to answer.json and printing the status and the content type
a python step printed the answer's keys, the JWT header and the JWT claims without jti
the same curl GET with the bearer wrong in place of the request token (WRONG_REQUEST_TOKEN=wrong in the step's env), printing the body, the status and the content type
